rules.statement: An API key grants nothing of its own: its memberships are its principal's, from the MembershipProvider, narrowed to the key's roles, so a key is never more than its principal.

A key's roles only narrow: with a cap, no role outside it (matched by space and role) reaches the key, and neither does an ALLOW of a directly attached policy or of a Principal binding; their DENYs apply to the key as to its principal (RC1-1). An empty cap leaves only what Anyone may do, less what the principal is denied.

A credential whose memberships come from the MembershipProvider (an API key, or a token marked cosec.membership: provider) is invalid when the provider does not know its principal or knows it as not active: the request is evaluated as anonymous and a deny is 401 token-invalid. A provider that fails is 503, never an unknown principal.
API keys turned on without a MembershipProvider bean fail startup, naming CoCacheMembershipProvider: a key's memberships are its principal's, and every key would otherwise be a 503.

A token that delegates (it carries an `act` claim, RFC 8693) never becomes a principal, however valid it is otherwise: the token is rejected as invalid, so the request is evaluated as anonymous and a deny answers 401 `token-invalid`. `may_act` does not delegate.

A gateway forwards the verified CoSec-Identity only to a route that receives it: one whose metadata cosec-identity is exactly true, or one without that metadata whose URI is a registered service (lb://, lb:ws://). Metadata false, or any other value, keeps it from the route whatever its URI, and so does a request no route marks: such a route's backend receives no identity.
guards: gateway:PipelineGatewayFilterTest#only a load-balanced route, or one marked true, receives the identity
runtime:IdentityForwardingTest#a request no route marks as receiving the identity forwards none

rules.statement: A gateway forwards none of the caller's credentials downstream unless cosec.gateway.identity.forward-authorization is on, and then only to a route that receives the identity (IDN-7): not the Authorization header, not the API key header under the name cosec.pipeline.api-key-header gives it, not the authorization query parameter, however its name is encoded or cased, and not the authorization cookie, however its name is cased or spaced, in any Cookie header: each is rewritten without it, the token's pair going with one ';' and the other pairs byte for byte, so no empty pair is made and only the whitespace at the head of the result goes, since a field value cannot start with it (a header whose leading $Version pair hides it behind a ',', or in which a kept $Version pair would come to the head, goes whole), and one left with only empty pairs, of whitespace and ',', is not sent; the cookies the request handed on reports (to a later filter, or a forward: route's handler) agree, a header that went whole taking its cookies with it.
properties: gateway:CookieTokenPropertyTest#no forwarded cookie header names the token, and every other cookie decodes as it did
guards: gateway:PipelineGatewayFilterTest#the caller's credentials stay at the gateway unless asked for, and then go only where the identity goes
runtime:QueryParametersTest#the authorization parameter goes, however its name is written
runtime:CookieHeadersTest#the authorization cookie goes, however its name is cased or spaced
runtime:CookieHeadersTest#kept pairs go on as they came
runtime:CookieHeadersTest#names reads a header in linear time
gateway:PipelineGatewayFilterTest#the cookies a later filter reads agree with the headers handed on

rules.statement: On a host that decides with policies (cosec.pipeline.mode=enforce), no adapter hands a handler a CoSec-Identity header a client sent: every permit of the pipeline strips it, and WebMvc, WebFlux and the gateway apply that alike. A service behind a gateway (mode gateway) keeps the header its gateway sent.
guards: spring-boot:WebAdapterParityTest#the three adapters hand on no client identity
runtime:IdentityForwardingTest#without an issuer a permit strips the client's identity and forwards none

rules.statement: An id with an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate is refused where it enters CoSec, so two different ids never share a stored key: a Redis key is UTF-8, which writes the surrogate as `?`, and tenant `beta\uD800` would read the documents, memberships and revocations of tenant `beta?`. A token that claims one in its subject, tenant, jti, roles or policies is invalid (401 token-invalid) before any revocation is read, and CoSec's token issuer refuses to sign one; a forwarded identity naming one is malformed (400); a control request holding one in its path, query or body is 400; an authenticator, an API key record or a membership provider that gives one has failed (503); cosec-migrate rejects a converted document that holds one (INVALID_ID), and publishes nothing. A surrogate pair is a character like any other. A rate limit key value with one counts in an escaped bucket of its own, never in another value's.
guards: model:IdentifiersTest#well formed is what survives UTF-8
runtime:UnpairedSurrogatePipelineTest#an authenticator whose principal holds an unpaired surrogate is unavailable
runtime:UnpairedSurrogatePipelineTest#a membership provider whose answer holds an unpaired surrogate is unavailable
runtime:IdentityCodecTest#an id with an unpaired surrogate is refused as malformed
control:ControlHttpTest#a request holding an unpaired surrogate is a 400, wherever it holds it
engine:RateLimitObligationTest#a key value with an unpaired surrogate counts in a well formed bucket of its own
model:ScopeResolverTest#a declared app that cannot be an app id is rejected with or without a host app
migrate:ConverterTest#an id with an unpaired surrogate is rejected, and nothing is converted

rules.statement: A token's tenant claim names a tenant or is absent. Absent, the principal is in the default tenant (0). An empty claim makes the token invalid (401 token-invalid) on every path that verifies one, the pipeline's and refresh's, whichever verifier read it: read as no tenant, it would put the principal in the default tenant with the token's roles. A claim that cannot name a tenant document (blank, `*`, holding `:` or a control character, longer than 128 characters: the rule of `SnapshotKey.Tenant`) makes the token invalid as well, and an API key record with such a tenant fails (503), so every credential applies one rule. CoSec's issuer refuses to sign a token with an empty tenant or one it would refuse.

An id beginning with ( is CoSec's, as the tenants (0) and (platform) and the space (default): a token whose subject begins with ( is invalid, on every path that verifies one, and none is issued. Whether a principal is authenticated is stated by the pipeline, never read off its id.

A refresh token (the claim cosec.token, which the converter writes as refresh) is invalid wherever an access token is expected, on every path that verifies one: signed and unexpired, it never authenticates as a principal, so a principal named after the access token's id cannot exist. A token without the claim is an access token, whoever issued it. The other way too: a refresh reads only a refresh token where one belongs, issued with the access token it is presented with (its sub is that token's jti, its iat that token's iat); an access token there is refused, so whoever holds a token of a principal named after another token's id cannot refresh that token.

A token is never issued on a revocation read that failed: a refresh whose revocations cannot be read (RevocationUnavailableException) fails, never reads the old token as not revoked, so a revoked token, or a token of a revoked principal, cannot be refreshed into one that no revocation names. The pipeline's degraded verification (PIP-7) applies to verifying a token only.
guards: jwt:SimpleRefreshTokenAuthenticationTest#a refresh is refused when the revocations cannot be read

rules.source: RFC 0009 (refresh token families, 2026-11-14 revision); round-2 review M2
rules.statement: Only a family's current generation moves it: a refresh of the current generation moves the family to its next generation with a conditional write of the record it read, so of concurrent refreshes of one pair exactly one moves it, on one instance or many. A refresh of any other generation never moves it.
guards: runtime:TokenFamiliesTest#refreshes of one pair racing move the family once
cocache:CoCacheTokenFamilyStoreTest#refreshes of one pair racing on two instances move the family once
jwt:RefreshTokenFamiliesJwtTest#a retried refresh heals, and only the current pair moves the session on

rules.source: RFC 0009 (refresh token families, 2026-11-14 revision); round-2 review M2
rules.statement: The generation the family just replaced, presented within cosec.jwt.session.rotation-leeway of the move, is answered with a pair of the current generation and moves nothing: a refresh whose response was lost can be retried, and two tabs refreshing one pair both keep a usable pair. The window opens at the move and does not slide. Any older generation, or the one just replaced after the leeway, revokes the whole family and is refused, so a copied pair, even one answered within the leeway, is caught at the next refresh after it.
guards: runtime:TokenFamiliesTest#the pair just replaced is answered at the current generation within the leeway
runtime:TokenFamiliesTest#a copy answered within the leeway is caught at the next refresh

rules.source: RFC 0009 (refresh token families, 2026-11-14 revision); round-2 review M2
rules.statement: A family ends cosec.jwt.session.lifetime after its login, however often it was refreshed: a refresh after that is refused and the user signs in again, no pair outlives that end, and a tenant switch, which does not sign the user in again, keeps the login time.
guards: runtime:TokenFamiliesTest#a family ends at its absolute lifetime
jwt:RefreshTokenFamiliesJwtTest#a pair never outlives its session
login:AbstractSwitchTenantAuthenticationTest#the new session keeps the login time of the token switched from

rules.source: RFC 0009 (refresh token families, 2026-11-14 revision); round-2 review M2
rules.statement: A logout ends the session: TokenRevoker revokes the family and the access token's id, from the access token while it is valid and from the pair (bound as a refresh requires) once it has expired, so no pair of the family refreshes afterwards, the pairs it was refreshed from included. The family is marked revoked, never deleted, until its end.
guards: runtime:TokenFamiliesTest#logout ends every pair of the family
cocache:CoCacheTokenFamilyStoreTest#logout on one instance ends the family on the other
jwt:RefreshTokenFamiliesJwtTest#logout ends every pair of the session

rules.source: RFC 0009 (refresh token families, 2026-11-14 revision); round-2 review M2
rules.statement: A family record that cannot be read, or a write of it that cannot be confirmed, issues nothing: the refresh fails (503), never reads the family as absent or the write as done. A missing record refuses the refresh (401).
guards: runtime:TokenFamiliesTest#an unreadable family record issues nothing
cocache:CoCacheTokenFamilyStoreTest#an unreadable family record issues nothing
cocache:CoCacheTokenFamilyStoreTest#the family table reads a failure as unknown, and no layer changes that

rules.statement: A social sign-in's callback is accepted only with a state CoSec issued, once, and only from the browser that started the sign-in: the state is taken from the SocialStateStore (removed atomically) before the provider is called, whatever follows, and the browser's binding must hash to the one recorded with the state. A callback whose state is unknown, expired, already used or issued to another browser is refused, and the provider is never called for it.

A principal's attributes cannot be changed once its authenticator has returned it: they are what the host reads from its SecurityContext and what every further check of the request decides on (subject.attributes.*). AuthenticatedPrincipal keeps a read-only view of the map it is handed, and CoSec's token verifier makes the attributes claim read-only at every level, nested objects and arrays included. A change through the principal, at any level, throws, and a further check decides as the first did; what is read is what the authenticator handed over.
